- Overestimate prices after recent sentiment spikes (especially when sentiment > 0.10) — model tends to overshoot and fail to correct quickly.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is negative or recently negative (sentiment < 0.05) — model is too optimistic, fails to reflect bearish momentum.
- Lag in price correction: model often delays downward adjustments after negative sentiment, especially if sentiment dips sharply.
- Mean reversion bias: model overreacts to short-term volatility, underestimating long-term trend reversion toward historical mean.
- Horizon-specific error: 30-day forecasts are consistently too high in early periods (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is positive, then overcorrect later.
- Avoid “sentiment echo” — model replicates sentiment direction without adjusting for actual price momentum or volume signals.
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive, model tends to overproject upward — reduce forecast slope if sentiment < 0.15.
- If sentiment is negative and price is rising, model often fails to recognize reversal — suppress upward bias in such cases.
